title: Identity and pasting laws of the sheaf-level square isomorphism
statement:
Let $u^{-1}$ denote the inverse image functors on abelian sheaves on small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], with the composition isomorphisms $c_{u,v}:v^{-1}u^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}(u\circ v)^{-1}$ (for $u:Y\to X$, $v:Z\to Y$) and the identity isomorphisms $e_X:\mathrm{id}_X^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition]. For a cartesian square $\square=(f,f',g,g',\alpha)$ [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] with $f:X\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $g:Y'\to Y$, $g':X'\to X$, let $\theta_\square:f'^{-1}g^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}g'^{-1}f^{-1}$ be its specified isomorphism, namely $\theta_\square=c_{f,g'}^{-1}\circ c_{g,f'}$, through $(g\circ f')^{-1}=(f\circ g')^{-1}$ (the two composites are the same morphism $X'\to Y$; this is the definition of the source Lean `AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.squareUpperStarIso`, attached to [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]). Outer rectangles of pasted cartesian squares are cartesian [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting]. Then:

1. (Identity square.) For $f:X\to Y$ and $\square_f=(f,f,\mathrm{id}_Y,\mathrm{id}_X)$: $\theta_{\square_f}=(e_X^{-1}f^{-1})\circ(f^{-1}e_Y):f^{-1}\mathrm{id}_Y^{-1}\to f^{-1}\to\mathrm{id}_X^{-1}f^{-1}$.
2. (Horizontal pasting.) For $\square_1=(f,f',g,g')$, a cartesian square $\square_2=(f',f'',h,h')$ with $h:Y''\to Y'$, $h':X''\to X'$, $f'':X''\to Y''$, and the outer rectangle $\square_2\cdot\square_1=(f,f'',g\circ h,g'\circ h')$:
$$\theta_{\square_2\cdot\square_1}\circ(f''^{-1}c_{g,h})=(c_{g',h'}f^{-1})\circ(h'^{-1}\theta_{\square_1})\circ(\theta_{\square_2}g^{-1}):\ f''^{-1}h^{-1}g^{-1}\to(g'h')^{-1}f^{-1}.$$
3. (Vertical pasting.) For $\square_1$ as above, a cartesian square $\square_3=(e,e',g',g'')$ with $e:W\to X$, $e':W'\to X'$, $g'':W'\to W$, and the outer rectangle $\square_1\circ\square_3=(f\circ e,f'\circ e',g,g'')$:
$$\theta_{\square_1\circ\square_3}\circ(c_{f',e'}g^{-1})=(g''^{-1}c_{f,e})\circ(\theta_{\square_3}f^{-1})\circ(e'^{-1}\theta_{\square_1}):\ e'^{-1}f'^{-1}g^{-1}\to g''^{-1}(fe)^{-1}.$$
(Only the equalities $fg'=gf'$ of the squares enter, not that they are cartesian.)
